name: Archeofuturism
summary: Archeofuturism, coined by Guillaume Faye in 1998, seeks to join modern technoscience to what he called archaic values: hierarchy, rootedness in ethnic and civilizational identity, and a pre-Christian spiritual outlook. It rejects egalitarianism, liberal democracy, consumer society and globalized finance, and favours an authoritarian leader, semi-autarchic blocs, an organic Third Way economy, a pan-European or Eurosiberian union, restriction of non-European immigration and natalist policy. Faye expected a convergence of catastrophes to end the modern order.
scope: The profile represents Guillaume Faye's own Archeofuturism (book of 1998 and the related Convergence of Catastrophes and Why We Fight) as documented by Wikipedia, scholars such as Stephane Francois, and sympathetic essays that quote him. It excludes later alt-right and identitarian uses of the term and the broader French New Right of Alain de Benoist, from whom Faye split. Many economic and social-policy statements were not addressed by Faye and are low-confidence inferences.

sources.title: Guillaume Faye
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Faye's career, conviction, authoritarian and ethno-nationalist positions and the idea of metapolitics.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from the call for a superior authority steering a communal "organic" economy; healthcare itself is not discussed, and the guarantee would serve natives rather than all comers.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage-setting is never discussed; the Third Way economy rejects both liberal and socialist wage logic, so adherents have no settled line.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Faye proposed an organic Third Way economy beyond liberalism, with a political authority directing the economy, and rejected economism.

public-ownership.rationale: The authority is to direct the economy without managing it, which points away from nationalisation, yet the Third Way is not laissez-faire; ownership forms are not specified.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation is not addressed; hostility to speculative finance suggests sympathy but the inegalitarian stance gives no reason to favour levelling.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not discussed; an organic, authority-led economy might favour corporatist bodies but not class unions, so the answer is split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred from the organic Third Way, which subordinates economic life to community and political authority rather than treating property as untouchable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The movement calls for prohibiting speculative and globalized capitalism, which implies tight political control over large firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare is not discussed; adherents oppose paying for immigrants but also favour communal solidarity and natalism, so they are split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the economy is to be directed from above in an organic order, not turned over to worker collectives, and Faye rejected socialism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian, identity-protecting regime and emergency powers Faye advocated; surveillance is not specifically discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the stress on biological and ethological hygiene and vitalism; drug policy itself is not discussed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Faye was convicted of incitement to racial hatred, so adherents regard such laws as persecution; the position is inferred from that history.

strong-leader.rationale: Faye promoted an authoritarian regime led by a charismatic "born chief" who would decide in emergencies.

state-harmful.rationale: Faye wanted a strong superior political authority, so the claim that the state is unnecessary is the opposite of his view.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the Darwinian struggle ethos and rejection of pacifism; gun control is not discussed.

empower-police-military.rationale: An authoritarian regime defending European identity against decline and catastrophe implies strong coercive institutions. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on hygiene and organic community over liberal individual choice; not discussed.

decide-locally.rationale: Faye treated regional and national grievances as counterproductive and wanted Europe-wide and Eurosiberian unity under a strong authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the hard, hierarchical, anti-humanitarian outlook; penal policy is not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Natalist policy and loyalty to bloodlines make family continuity a pillar of the archaic values Faye wanted restored.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from archaic, bloodline-centred values; the source does not address it and some adherents are indifferent.

abortion-legal.rationale: Natalism argues against abortion, but eugenic selection and anti-Christian morality argue for choice, so adherents are split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Faye wanted a rooted pagan spirituality but opposed Christianity and Islam, so a generic larger religious role is not endorsed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Faye condemned "ethnomasochism", the self-hatred of one's own ethnic group, and rejected anti-racist guilt politics.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from biological determinism and the claim that archaic values are grounded in nature; not discussed in the sources.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Identity preservation is central, though the unit Faye cares about is the European and Eurosiberian people more than the single nation.

gradual-change.rationale: The aim is a change of civilization and not merely of regime, in the face of expected catastrophes.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Faye argued against immigration and called for non-European immigrants to return to their civilizational areas.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Faye opposed Western universalism and standardization of the world and favoured civilizational blocs.

free-trade.rationale: The movement calls for economic autarky and for banning globalized capitalism.

nation-first.rationale: Semi-autarchic blocs and opposition to globalization imply putting the bloc's interest first, though the bloc is Europe or Eurosiberia.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from rejection of universalism and of human-rights egalitarianism; interventions to protect others are not endorsed.

open-borders.rationale: Faye opposed immigration and advocated return of non-Europeans, the reverse of open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Faye rejected consumer society and warned of pollution but embraced technoscience for growth, so adherents are split.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Faye listed uncontrolled pollution among threats but climate policy is not discussed; an authoritarian regime might act, but he favoured techno solutions.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Faye wanted technoscience joined to archaic values, not technology alone, and expected collapse; inferred as partial disagreement.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from keeping advanced techno-industrial capacity in the new order while consuming energy at scale.

revolution-justified.rationale: A change of civilization rather than regime, via metapolitics and expected catastrophe, implies radical rupture is acceptable. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

experts-over-public.rationale: The movement attacks "the System" as replacing democracy with technocracy, though rule by a born chief is not rule by the public either.

central-planning.rationale: The authority should direct the economy without managing it, an organic Third Way short of full central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Markets under communal or state ownership are not discussed; the Third Way is undefined on this.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on lineage and bloodlines; inheritance taxation is not discussed.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from rejection of egalitarian redistribution and of the consumer society.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic autarky is demanded, which implies protection of domestic and bloc industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: A superior political authority is to direct the economy, which implies steering strategic investment. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not discussed; organic economy language could favour it but nothing documents it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Faye proposed an organic Third Way beyond socialism and kept a hierarchical economy, so abolishing money and wage labor is rejected.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Hostility to speculative finance is documented, but central banks specifically are not discussed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the organic Third Way and a directing authority; no corporatist program is cited.

one-party-rule.rationale: Faye wanted a charismatic chief, not a party guided by doctrine; the party form is not documented.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Faye expected neo-feudal networks and a born chief; monarchy as such is not endorsed.

democracy-best.rationale: Faye rejected liberal democracy in favour of a leader-centred order.

direct-votes.rationale: Not documented; a charismatic chief may use plebiscites, but nothing is cited.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred from rejection of socialism and egalitarian doctrine.

right-to-secede.rationale: Faye treated regional grievances as counterproductive and wanted larger unions.

natural-rulers.rationale: The movement affirms inequality of value between men and a born, providential chief.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Darwinian struggle of the fittest and a clash of civilizations leave no room for absolute pacifism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Faye adopted a Darwinian struggle of the fittest and saw peoples in conflict, which implies struggle strengthens. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

separate-church-state.rationale: Faye wanted rooted pagan spirituality in the culture but no church establishment is documented.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Archeofuturism seeks a post-Christian, pre-Christian-rooted life form and opposes scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from the demand for a strong superior authority.

military-superiority.rationale: Faye described international relations as struggle among peoples and civilizations, so strength is required.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Europe is defined as peoples related by blood ties, history and culture, and Faye promoted ethnic biological roots.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Faye wanted a Third Way beyond socialism and saw civilizational and ethnic conflict, not class, as central.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The movement openly rejects egalitarianism and affirms inequality between persons and peoples.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on ethnic rootedness and identity; indigenous peoples are not discussed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of ethnomasochism and guilt politics.

civilizational-union.rationale: Faye envisioned Eurosiberia, uniting the peoples of Europe and the former Soviet Union.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred from a holistic communal ethos, though the Darwinian struggle theme pulls the other way.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Faye favoured a holistic, organic society over Western individualist universalism.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The movement invokes vitalism and ethological principles, though nature's intrinsic value is not a stated tenet.

limit-population.rationale: Faye was natalist for Europeans while alarmed by other regions' demography, so there is no uniform answer.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Faye saw modernity as obsolete but wanted to keep technoscience, so a flat verdict of disaster is rejected.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The project reconciles technoscience with archaic values and treats modern institutions as obsolete.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from the eugenicist and technoscientific outlook.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule by a born chief, and criticism of technocracy, argue against delegating government to algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Faye wrote before mass encryption debates and the sources show no view; his authoritarian state favours surveillance while his anti-System stance favours private communication, so no lean.

restore-past-order.rationale: Faye said the future must be archaic, neither modern nor attached to the past, rejecting plain restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred from the movement's explicit worldview and aesthetic of politics.

direct-action.rationale: Faye favoured metapolitical cultural change and infiltration; the direct action versus elections question is not documented.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred from the metapolitical strategy of cultural change toward an authoritarian end, not mirroring the ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The core idea is to keep technoscience while restoring archaic foundations, not to abandon civilization.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred from a hierarchical society with a techno elite and a traditional majority.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The movement rejects egalitarianism and affirms inequality of value.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from the Third Way economy, which is neither profit-driven liberalism nor socialism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Faye rejected socialism and Marxist analysis, treating the economy as organic.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Faye rejected socialism and egalitarianism and favoured a born chief.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of socialism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Faye saw conflict as grounded in peoples and civilizations rather than economic systems.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred from the demand for a strong directing authority.

harm-principle.rationale: Biological and ethological hygiene principles and civilizational goals override the liberal limit on state power.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Faye favoured a holistic, organic society and rejected Western universalism.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from the struggle ethos and authoritarian identity-defending state.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from rejection of liberal individualism.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from the call for political authority above economic logic.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from rejection of both liberalism and socialism; freedom as material means is not an Archeofuturist theme.

media-academia-power.rationale: The movement attacks "the System" and its anti-fascism; media and academia are implied but not named.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Faye endorsed a differentialist hierarchy between peoples and ethnic biological roots.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from the organic society and neo-feudal network ideas.

total-state.rationale: The authority directs the economy without managing it, short of a total state.

national-rebirth.rationale: The aim is a change of civilization out of decline, with the people regenerating after catastrophe, though framed as European.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred from struggle among peoples and the Eurosiberian project.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Faye expected neo-feudal networks; oaths of loyalty are inferred from that.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred: neo-feudal networks are expected but legal serfdom is not endorsed.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Metapolitics assumes culture shapes power, yet adherents also claim objective biological facts, so split.

universal-morality.rationale: Faye opposed Western universalism and favoured differentialism.

single-common-good.rationale: Inferred from the holistic organic society and a chief who decides for the people.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Faye later treated Israel as a potential ally against Muslims, though earlier hostile; inferred modest agreement.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from the idea that peoples belong in their civilizational areas.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is never raised in the sources; Faye's unit is the European or Eurosiberian people, not a single national tongue.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from rejection of egalitarian socialism.

school-vouchers.rationale: School funding mechanisms are absent from the sources; the movement's concern is cultural identity in education, not who pays.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal deficits are not discussed; Faye warned of financial crises but gave no budget rule.

economic-freedom.rationale: Faye placed politics above economics and rejected economism.

rule-by-example.rationale: A charismatic, providential chief who embodies identity fits this, though not documented as a doctrine.

national-self-determination.rationale: Differentialism gives each people its own space, but the Eurosiberian bloc supersedes national statehood.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from anti-universalism and struggle among civilizations.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The movement invokes will to power, vitalism and pre-Christian spirituality rather than reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Opposition to immigration and a focus on native peoples imply welfare for natives only.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the Darwinian, anti-egalitarian outlook.

class-collaboration.rationale: The organic Third Way economy rejects class struggle in favour of communal order.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The archaic means foundations and ancestral values, so inherited culture is not to be sacrificed.

dominated-front.rationale: Faye wanted Europe separate from the West yet saw other civilizations as enemies, so no front with them.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred from the people-based rather than class-based view of solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from biologically grounded archaic values; not documented in the sources opened.

ban-interest.rationale: The movement calls for banning speculative capitalism; interest bans are not stated.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Faye wanted remigration to civilizational areas rather than domestic legal segregation, and adherents differ.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy sources are not discussed in the sources; the technoscience emphasis and the pollution concern point in opposite directions.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Faye held that biological roots make assimilation unrealistic and urged return instead.

elite-replacement.rationale: The movement describes immigration as a deliberate strategy flooding the indigenous European population.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is irrelevant to a movement that rejects parliamentary democracy for a born chief.

national-mission.rationale: Faye opposed Western universalism and the export of its model.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of egalitarian gender doctrine.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The movement treats the ruling "System" as hostile to European identity.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Faye promoted natalist and eugenicist policies.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian and emergency-powers outlook.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Faye wanted a superior authority directing the economy and society.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Faye held a racialist view of biological roots and called multiracial society conflictual.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The movement endorses inequality of value between men and a hierarchy between peoples.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The statement is about Marxist socialism, which Faye rejected, so no considered stance.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not discussed; Faye's civilizational view cuts both ways.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from a unified identity and anti-multicultural outlook.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not discussed; Faye opposed Islam but championed pagan spirituality, which is not about conversion law.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred from a vitalist, non-vegetarian European pagan outlook.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Faye wanted rooted pagan spirituality but opposed Christianity and Islam, and no source addresses religious teaching in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Faye rejected socialism, and the premise is Marxist.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Faye rejected liberal democracy in favour of a born chief, so legitimacy rests on providential leadership more than consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Faye called for non-European immigrants to return to their civilizational areas.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A Darwinian struggle worldview rejects an absolute ban on initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Faye adopted a Darwinian struggle of the fittest and saw civilizations in conflict.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Faye was prosecuted for his writings and criticized the System's repression, so adherents oppose such bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican freedom concept is not part of the movement; inferred from authoritarian preferences.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred from the single born chief with emergency decision power.

vanguard-party.rationale: The metapolitical elite idea parallels a vanguard but is not a disciplined revolutionary party; no documented stance.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not addressed; the Third Way economy gives no stance on council housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Industrial relations law is not discussed; an authoritarian state would curb strikes while the organic economy favours class peace, with nothing documented.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Faye was alarmed by extra-European demography; inferred partial agreement.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Faye described a multiracial society as inherently conflictual ("multiracist").

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rule by a born chief and inequality of value oppose random selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The born chief is to take emergency decisions to protect identity.

party-controls-media.rationale: The movement criticizes the System's media; party control is not a stated tenet.

party-commands-army.rationale: The ruler is a chief, not a party; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Faye opposed immigration and treated ethnic descent as the basis of belonging.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of elected officials is not discussed, and a movement hostile to parliaments has no stated line on it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party internal rules are not addressed, as the movement is metapolitical and centred on a leader rather than a party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Faye supported European integration, though of a different kind than the EU.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The born chief holds decisive authority including emergency decisions.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred from the anti-Christian, pre-Christian spiritual orientation.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement is post-Christian and treats Islam as an enemy, rejecting clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred from the struggle of peoples and a strong nation-bloc outlook.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Politics is treated as aesthetics but censorship for virtue is not documented.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from a lifelong providential chief.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of elected officials is a democratic mechanism the sources never mention; Faye's preferred regime avoids elections.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Faye separated Europe from "the West" and sought a Eurosiberian bloc, implying autonomy from US alliances.

people-in-arms.rationale: Faye's sources discuss struggle among peoples but never propose a citizen militia versus a professional army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The archaic majority living traditionally is imagined, yet technoscience cities persist; adherents are split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred from the pan-European and Eurosiberian unity goal.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from attacks on the System and its intellectual class.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Faye endorsed a differentialist hierarchy between peoples and viewed other civilizations as rivals.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian and emergency-powers outlook.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from rejection of gender equality doctrine.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The movement is pagan and Darwinian, not creationist.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the hygiene and vitalism themes.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Europe is defined by blood ties, and belonging rests on ethnic descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Faye treated regionalist grievances as counterproductive.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from hostility to Islam and uniform identity.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the organic, holistic society over liberal individualism.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief for poor countries is not in the sources; Faye saw the global South as a rival bloc, not a debtor to be helped.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The statement concerns decolonization and has no counterpart in Faye's Europe-centred writing.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from rejection of liberal democracy.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian, technoscientific project.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Faye wanted civilizations separated and saw the South as a rival bloc.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from Europe as an autonomous strategic bloc.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: A providential chief with popular acclaim is closer to this than to parliamentary election, but not documented.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred from the demand for political authority above finance.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial peace settlements are not discussed for any region in the sources opened.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Third Way organic economy subordinates economic life to the community.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union's class character is a Marxist debate that Faye did not take part in.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not discussed beyond a general worry about pollution.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the Eurosiberian bloc concept.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International-law questions about annexation are not addressed in the sources.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A chief above factional politics fits, though not stated this way.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from opposing regional grievances and valuing unity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not discussed; semi-autarchic blocs with different production modes hint at it but not within one state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The chief is providential, but divine descent is not claimed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax rate structure is never discussed in the sources.

character-from-environment.rationale: Faye held to biological roots and inequality of value, opposing environmental determinism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from the chief who makes emergency decisions.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from the technoscientific, future-oriented side.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not cited; Faye's born chief is closer to one-man rule, but no source compares constitutions.

leader-cult.rationale: A charismatic providential chief implies public honour, inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed in the sources; natalism and traditional roles pull in different directions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This is an internal Marxist-Leninist question outside Faye's Third Way.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from hostility to immigration and rejection of guilt narratives.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Eurosiberia unites peoples by ethnicity across borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Rooted in anti-Islamic and pagan outlook; punishing apostasy is not endorsed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Faye treated Islam as an enemy of Europe, so imposing Islamic dress rules is rejected.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from support for European integration.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Faye's Eurosiberia unites related European and Russian peoples.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from separating peoples into civilizational areas.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Faye grounded history in will, identity and biological roots and criticised economism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed; hostility to speculative capitalism does not translate into antitrust views.

no-bailouts.rationale: The movement attacks speculative capitalism but bailouts are not discussed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from attacks on the System's institutions.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from rejection of egalitarian doctrine.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky and semi-autarchic blocs are explicit, though the statement's colonial element is not.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from preference for autarky over multilateral trade regimes.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive systems for labor are not discussed in the sources.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Faye's strategy was metapolitical, not armed vanguard; no explicit view.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inequality and lineage values run through the movement.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Identity, roots and civilization as foundation imply teaching one's own heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Faye wanted civilizations apart rather than rule over others.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on identity and roots.

public-money-creation.rationale: Faye attacked speculative finance, but the sources give no position on who should create money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Faye warned of recurring global financial crises.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence is not discussed; Eurosiberia is a bloc project rather than a legacy-empire claim.

delink-world-market.rationale: Autarky language concerns Europe's bloc; no view on poor countries.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Marxist thesis about workers in rich countries is not addressed by Faye.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the political primacy over economy and communal order.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from rejection of liberal constitutionalism.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaties are not discussed in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Faye favored a born chief rather than election.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from deference to a providential chief.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from rejection of liberal democracy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not addressed in the sources; vitalism and hygiene themes give no direction.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from vitalist, non-egalitarian view of nature.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: A hierarchical society with elites implies duty, inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Faye rejects liberal democracy and favours an authoritarian leader linked directly to the people.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed; archaic hierarchy and a modern outlook pull in opposite directions.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the semi-autarchic blocs and rejection of globalized finance, which favour control of resources by the bloc.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Faye's organic Third Way economy rejects egalitarianism but this specific question of process versus pattern is not addressed; inferred from his hierarchical, anti-egalitarian stance.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not discussed in these terms; inferred from Faye's rejection of egalitarian and anti-racist ideology, which he treated as an ideology of the decaying modern order.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from Faye's hierarchical, authoritarian outlook, which puts the sovereign leader's order above individual conscience, though he never addressed natural-law arguments.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Faye wanted technoscience placed at the service of a people's power, but he also stressed work, hierarchy and rootedness and never addressed shorter hours; adherents have no settled line.

multipolar-world.rationale: Faye called for a world of semi-autarchic blocs and a Eurosiberian union able to stand alongside other civilizational powers rather than under American hegemony.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: His organic Third Way economy rejects both liberal and Marxist economics, so a labour theory of value is not part of his thought; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Faye celebrated rootedness and loyalty to one's own people and favoured a communal economy, but he rejected international solidarity; only half the statement fits, so the answer is inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Faye was hostile to the left as a whole and put identity and civilization first, so the question of what the left should do is outside his frame; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Faye favoured an organic mixed economy under an authoritarian leader, not communist party rule; the question is outside his discussion and the answer is inferred.

missingStatements.text: Modern technological civilization should be combined with a return to ancestral values rather than choosing one over the other.
missingStatements.rationale: This synthesis of technoscience and archaic values is the defining thesis of Faye's book.

missingStatements.text: A people's economic life should be organised in semi-self-sufficient blocs of peoples rather than a single global market.
missingStatements.rationale: Faye and his adherents call for autarky and semi-autarchic blocs with differing modes of production.

missingStatements.text: Western civilization and Europe are distinct, and Europeans should define themselves apart from the West.
missingStatements.rationale: The essay separates Europe, a gathering of related peoples, from the West; Faye's Eurosiberia is the corresponding project.
missingStatements.declined: Idiosyncratic to one thinker's Europe/West distinction; the civilizational statements (civilizational-union, institutions-fit-civilization) already capture the civilizational dimension.

notes: Statements on economics, family, criminal justice and many others were not addressed by Faye and were answered as low-confidence inferences. Wikipedia reports Faye's views as read by scholars who describe them as racist and authoritarian.
